hypotheses.reasoning: The fault originates at the external identity provider (https://idp.example/oauth2/token). Its latency climbs from about 2s at 22:04:41 (#638, 4271ms) to 11.9s at 22:05:23 (#671), then calls hang with no response within 30s (#685) and fail with upstream timeouts (#768). auth-svc is otherwise healthy beforehand: /tokens calls succeed in 25-90ms and GC is normal, so the auth-svc side is not the trigger. account-svc then times out calling auth-svc /tokens (#687, #769), its connection pool to auth-svc saturates (#845, 50/50 with 28 queued) and pool checkouts time out (#903). edge-proxy returns POST /login 503s (#796, #924, #948, #1022), which is what paged. The 503s, pool saturation and timeouts are downstream spread and are not cited as root-cause evidence. Analytics 429s are a separate, earlier, unrelated issue; they are not on the login path.
The IdP could be treated as an external outage, but it hung rather than failing fast or reporting itself down, which points to dependency_timeout. Included as a lower-ranked alternative only.

verdict.recommendedAction: Escalate to the identity provider owner: idp.example/oauth2/token is hanging, with latency rising from 22:04:41 and calls timing out at 30s. Short term, lower the auth-svc IdP call timeout well below 30s and add a fail-fast circuit breaker so account-svc stops queuing behind hung calls. Consider raising or bounding the account-svc to auth-svc connection pool. Separately, investigate the analytics-ingest 429 storm dropping events (analytics-forwarder, 21:59 onward), which is not the cause of the login failures.
